items: Dates and times now follow your choice under the font picker (ISO 2026-11-22 by default, or your region's style), everywhere in the app.
Speech recognition listens in your own variety of English (for example British or Australian) when your device is set to it.

Just speak now shows your score as you go: a large “Score so far” number, a live score for the part you are speaking, and trend lines — one chart for the overall score, and three for its components (voice, melody & flow, words), each switchable between your running score and the score of each part. The same charts are in the review.

Just speak is now an open-ended sitting: no topic and no time limit. Talk or read a book aloud for as long as you like — an hour is fine — pausing with Space or simply stopping for a break; long silences are not counted.
While you speak you see your speaking time, a score for every 2 minutes so far, and a nudge if your pace, energy or pitch starts to drift.
At the end you get a full review: every score charted across the sitting, your strongest and weakest stretches with playback from that spot, and halves, thirds and quarters.
Tick “I am reading a book aloud” and word choice and fillers are left out of the score, since the words are the author's.
If the page closes mid-sitting, the app offers to recover everything scored up to the last 2 minutes.

Themes now match every other app on this site: System (follows your device), Light, Dark, Midnight, Slate, Ocean, Forest, Ember, Gold, Synthwave, Terminal, Paper, Pastel, Mono and High contrast, under Settings → Theme. Your old theme was moved to the closest match once; the old Aurora and Paper defaults now follow your device again.

SpeechImprover now speaks 16 more languages (French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Croatian, German, Chinese, Ukrainian, Esperanto, Swahili, Hindi, Bengali, Indonesian, Urdu, Farsi and Arabic): pick one under Settings → Theme → Language. These are machine translations, and the menus, header and dashboard come first — more screens will follow.

AI speech review: through Cowork Sync, an AI coach can now grade each of your takes (A–F with strengths, fixes and what to try next). You review each grade before it's saved; it appears on the take beside the app's own score and can be undone.
While Google Drive sync is on, your Google picture now sits at the top of the app on every screen, so you can always see which account is syncing. Tap it to open the sync settings.
Long transcripts no longer push the buttons off the screen: they show the first few lines with a Show all button.
Every attribute score now shows ▲/▼ against your last take on the same exercise.
The halves / thirds / quarters table now scores every attribute in each part — not just pace — with the change from the first part to the last, so you can see what held up and what faded.

Cowork Sync: replies from your AI coach now wait for you to review them (tick which exercises to keep) before anything changes, can be undone from the run history, and each channel can run on a schedule.
The app now starts in light or dark to match your device, until you pick a theme yourself.
Streaks and the activity calendar now go by your own local day, so late-evening practice counts for today.
Settings → Erase everything on this device removes all of SpeechImprover's data here, and leaves your Google Drive copy alone.
When Google Drive sync is on, Settings shows your Google picture and name.
Everything now loads from the app's own site: no outside font or code services.
New default font (Atkinson Hyperlegible), with a font choice under Settings → Theme.
Longer takes are split into halves, thirds or quarters, with a grade for how well you held your pace.
After each take: how it compares with your last try at the same exercise, your best on it, and today's streak.
After reading a passage, Drill the misses gives you a quick drill of the words you misread or skipped.
Press Space on the results screen to go again.
Just speak: one click (sidebar, dashboard or Ctrl-K) and you're recording free speech after a 3-2-1.
Voice Lab → Echo practice plays your voice back a moment late through headphones, to help you slow down and articulate.
Reading passages have a Listen first button that reads the text aloud with the current word underlined.
Free speaking has a talk-length picker, and the timer turns green, yellow and red like a speaking club's timing lights.
Results show how your pace changed over the take.
Hedging words like “I think”, “maybe” and “just” are marked in free-speech transcripts.
Reading passages show words correct per minute.
